recentItems.title: Brooklyn News Today: Deadly shooting, massive fire and school slashing
recentItems.description:
Brooklyn investigators are searching for answers after 18-year-old Jayden Velasquez, known as “Gekko,” was shot and killed in Williamsburg just hours before he was set to begin his senior year of high school. The roundup also includes a large fire at a recycling yard on Maspeth Avenue in East Williamsburg, a student slashed inside a Fort Greene school on the first day of classes, the sentencing of Hakeem Smith in the murder of Douglas Young, an animal cruelty investigation after multiple cats were found dead in Bath Beach, a death following a medical episode in police custody, and child care workers rallying over delayed paychecks.

recentItems.title: Bronx News Today: Bronx health alert for Legionnaires’ outbreak, murder case and 911 questions
recentItems.description:
A Legionnaires’ disease outbreak in the South Bronx has left one person dead and five others diagnosed as health officials investigate at least 20 cooling towers that tested positive for bacteria in Melrose and Morrisania. The roundup also includes a Bronx murder defendant pleading not guilty in the fatal shooting of his niece, a not guilty plea in the deadly New York Harbor boat crash case, a rollover crash near the Hutchinson Parkway, updates for families displaced by a Norwood fire, new bus-lane camera enforcement on the BX11 and BX17 routes, and the opening of the Bronx School of Hip Hop’s inaugural school year.

recentItems.title: The search dogs of 9/11: How veterinarians kept ground zero rescuers going
recentItems.description:
As search-and-rescue teams worked through the wreckage of Ground Zero after the September 11 attacks, rescue dogs faced dangerous conditions, injuries, and exhaustion. At the request of the NYPD, the Suffolk County SPCA brought a mobile veterinary hospital directly to the scene to care for the animals. Veterinarians ultimately treated roughly 350 search-and-rescue and therapy dogs, helping them continue their critical mission.

recentItems.title: Brooklyn caretaker devastated after at least 7 cats found dead
recentItems.description:
At least seven cats were found dead under a deck in Bath Beach, Brooklyn, prompting an investigation by the NYPD's Animal Cruelty Investigation Squad. The ASPCA's forensics team is working with police as authorities try to determine the cause of death. The man who cared for the cats says he fears even more have died and is devastated by the loss.

recentItems.title: Brooklyn teen killed hours before senior year start in Williamsburg shooting
recentItems.description:

Friends affectionately called him “Gekko” and said he was well known around the neighborhood. The shooting happened just before 10 p.m. Wednesday outside 160 Havemeyer St.

recentItems.title: Connecticut News Today: 9/11 tribute, Holocaust memorial, bitcoin kidnapping sentence
recentItems.description:

recentItems.title: Hudson Valley News Today: Deadly fire kills 28-year-old, drug bust, assault indictment
recentItems.description:
A 28-year-old man has died following a three-alarm fire on Cedar Street in Yonkers that spread to a neighboring home and left two others injured. Authorities are also announcing felony drug charges against Poughkeepsie man Phillip Farrar, who investigators say sold cocaine from a North Perry Street apartment. In other cases, White Plains resident Micah Jackson was indicted on allegations he assaulted and strangled his former girlfriend in Yonkers, two suspects were arrested in connection with burglaries and grand larcenies in Harrison, and Poughkeepsie City Council member Christopher Grant faces an attempted assault charge.
